entries.text:
I'm trying to untangle the timeline here—figuring out whether the ledger viewer work happened before or after the a9a97ab commit relative to the compaction point and the user's prompt timestamp.

I suspect 558441a's 15 actions represent the actual viewer build, but the matching logic falls apart because the commit action at 11:59:42 already shows sha 00b9a06 and gets skipped, so the real boundary must come from an earlier action that merely mentions "git commit" in its text without actually being a commit.

The real fix is to let an action carry multiple SHAs via a global regex, since a single command printed both commits and my regex only grabbed the first one — that explains the duplicate segment issue. I'll need to reset my local agent-ledger branch back to 2707c31 and re-sync those entries, since it's safe local-only work from this session, then explain this briefly to the user before doing it.



Found a bug: a single `git commit` call produced two commits, but only the first SHA was captured, causing the second commit to be mismatched by time. Fixing it now.
